en.name: Energy requirement
en.shortDescription: Energy requirement — the target amount of energy a patient needs over 24 hours; in kilocalories (kcal).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Energy requirement is the *target* amount of energy a patient needs (estimated or prescribed), against which actual intake is compared. It produces a numeric value, typically per 24 hours, used to set nutritional goals. It is reported in kilocalories (kcal). It is a goal/estimate — not a measurement of what was delivered (that is *Energy intake*).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED *Energy requirement* concept with its descendants, grouped below for readability — all are the same `energy_requirement` target variable, in kcal.

### Generic energy requirement (default)

- *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement (SNOMED)*: the default target.
- *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours (SNOMED)*: the estimated 24-hour requirement.

### Population-specific

- *45771253 / 702387006 — Pediatric energy requirement (SNOMED)*: paediatric target.

## Excluded Concepts

Two descendants of the anchor are excluded because they are a different variable:

- *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours (SNOMED)*: expressed in kcal/kg/24 h, a different unit.
- *4027088 / 226245008 — Non-protein energy requirement (SNOMED)*: the share of the requirement not covered by protein, a quantity of its own.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a nutritional energy *target/goal* here, using *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* (SNOMED) by default.
- **The 24-hour estimate and the paediatric requirement are more specific forms**: map to them only when the source explicitly records that form; otherwise use the generic concept.
- Do **not** map energy actually delivered/consumed here — that is the *Energy intake* set.

fr.name: Besoin énergétique
fr.shortDescription: Besoin énergétique — quantité d'énergie cible nécessaire au patient sur 24 heures ; en kilocalories (kcal).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le besoin énergétique est la quantité *cible* d'énergie dont un patient a besoin (estimée ou prescrite), à laquelle l'apport réel est comparé. Il produit une valeur numérique, typiquement par 24 heures, servant à fixer les objectifs nutritionnels. Il est exprimé en kilocalories (kcal). C'est un objectif/une estimation — pas une mesure de ce qui a été délivré (cela relève d'*Energy intake*).

## Concepts inclus

Le jeu est ancré sur le concept SNOMED *Energy requirement* et ses descendants, regroupés ci-dessous pour la lisibilité — tous constituent la même variable cible `energy_requirement`, en kcal.

### Besoin énergétique générique (par défaut)

- *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement (SNOMED)* : la cible par défaut.
- *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours (SNOMED)* : le besoin estimé sur 24 heures.

### Spécifique à une population

- *45771253 / 702387006 — Pediatric energy requirement (SNOMED)* : cible pédiatrique.

## Concepts exclus

Deux descendants de l'ancre sont exclus car ils correspondent à une autre variable :

- *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours (SNOMED)* : exprimé en kcal/kg/24 h, une unité différente.
- *4027088 / 226245008 — Non-protein energy requirement (SNOMED)* : la part du besoin non couverte par les protéines, une grandeur à part entière.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici une *cible/objectif* énergétique nutritionnel, via *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* (SNOMED) par défaut.
- **Le besoin estimé sur 24 heures et le besoin pédiatrique sont des formes plus spécifiques** : ne mapper vers elles que si la source enregistre explicitement cette forme ; sinon utiliser le concept générique.
- Ne **pas** mapper ici l'énergie réellement délivrée/consommée — c'est le jeu *Energy intake*.

reviews.comments:
## Summary
**Needs revision.** Our indicator (QI03) uses only 604877 (Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours). Suggest to restrict the set to this concept: 604878 (per kg body weight), 4027088 (non-protein) and 45771253 (paediatric) denote different quantities, and the parent 4022415 (Energy requirement) is unspecific.

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI03 (Feeding).
- CQL: 1 of 5 concepts are referenced in [`IndicateQi03Feeding.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi03Feeding.cql?plain=1): [604877](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi03Feeding.cql?plain=1#L28) (each ID links to its code definition).

## Suggestions
- Restrict the expression to 604877 (Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours).

reviews.comments:
**Reply to the review of Gregor Lichtner**

Agreed:
- Remove **604878** *Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours*: different unit (kcal/kg/24 h).
- Remove **4027088** *Non-protein energy requirement*: a subset of the energy requirement, which would need its own concept set.

Needs discussion:
- **Keep 4022415** *Energy requirement*? A concept set gathers one clinical concept at every level of granularity: if a data provider mapped to the generic concept, its data should still be captured. Dropping it would mean renaming the set to target *Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours* only. A project that needs only the 24-hour estimate can filter that concept within the set.
- **Keep 45771253** *Pediatric energy requirement*? Same clinical concept, same dimension (kcal). Age groups are not split into separate sets: heart rate, for instance, is one set for newborns, children and adults, even though the values differ.

A concept set = one clinical concept, at the granularity used in research protocols, with one dimension (unit).

What do you think?
